featured_videos.title: Give Me 7 Minutes, I'll Save You 11 Years Of Carnivore Mistakes
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Elizabeth Bright
featured_videos.editorial_title: 11 Years of Carnivore Mistakes in 7 Minutes
featured_videos.commentary: Dr. Elizabeth Bright packed a lot into seven minutes and the comment section spent about 659 comments unpacking it further, mostly arguing about butter and OMAD timing. The video hits the common early mistakes that almost everyone makes, and the reason it's resonating is because experienced carnivores are showing up to say "yes, I did exactly this." It's the kind of content that works as a reset button for people who've been at it a while and feel stuck, not just a beginner primer. If you've been carnivore for more than a year and things have plateaued, this one is worth your seven minutes.

featured_videos.title: Heart Surgeon Says CARNIVORE is a DISASTER, PLEASE do NOT EAT CARNIVORE
featured_videos.creator: HomeSteadHow
featured_videos.commentary: A heart surgeon goes viral warning people away from carnivore, and the comment section turns into a peer-reviewed rebuttal from actual patients. The video highlights a real tension in medicine: population-level cholesterol guidelines versus the individual metabolic data that many carnivore eaters are collecting on themselves. The research on LDL in the context of low triglycerides and high HDL is more complicated than a single warning can capture, and the 1,260 comments reflect that people know it. What's worth watching here isn't the surgeon. It's how an informed community pushes back with labs, timelines, and before-and-after health markers.

featured_videos.title: We Discovered The Best Way To Make A Zero Carb Pizza Crust!
featured_videos.creator: Keto Twins
featured_videos.editorial_title: The Zero Carb Pizza Crust Carnivores Actually Want
featured_videos.commentary: The Keto Twins found something that got 48,000 people interested in a pizza crust, which is a sentence I didn't expect to write this week but here we are. The video walks through their zero carb base and the comments are full of people trying variations and reporting back, which is exactly the kind of recipe community energy that keeps things fun. It's landing the same week Reddit's carnivore pizza posts are stacking up upvotes, so the timing is perfect. Whether you're strict carnivore or just zero carb curious, this is the kind of creative problem-solving that makes the lifestyle feel a lot less restrictive.

featured_videos.title: Diabetes Reversed in 60 Days with Meat & Eggs~Carnivore for the WIN!
featured_videos.creator: Appalachia's Homestead with Patara
featured_videos.editorial_title: T2 Diabetes Reversed on Carnivore in 60 Days
featured_videos.commentary: James reversed a type 2 diabetes diagnosis in 60 days on a meat-and-eggs diet, and this video walks through exactly how that happened. The mechanism isn't mysterious: eliminating dietary carbohydrates drops postprandial glucose spikes, reduces insulin demand, and gives a chronically overworked pancreas time to recover. What makes this story worth paying attention to is that 60 days is fast, fast enough to show up in bloodwork before most doctors expect any meaningful change. If you've been told diabetes is permanent, that framing deserves a second look.

featured_videos.title: Everyone Is Quitting Carnivore (Here's Why)
featured_videos.creator: Professor Bart Kay - Nutrition and Health Science
featured_videos.commentary: Professor Bart Kay's breakdown on carnivore dropouts hit 540 comments this week, a 3x engagement ratio compared to most videos in the space. High comment counts mean people have strong opinions, which means the quitting problem is real and personal. The protocol isn't failing them. Their systems are. Watch this one if you're hitting a wall, then build a 30-day tracking system before you make any decisions about quitting.

featured_videos.title: Carnivore On A Budget: Is It Possible?
featured_videos.creator: Shawn Baker MD
featured_videos.editorial_title: Carnivore on a Budget: What the Numbers Say
featured_videos.commentary: The idea that carnivore is expensive is one of the most common reasons people don't try it, and Shawn Baker's breakdown challenges that assumption directly with real numbers. Commenters are reporting they're spending less per week on carnivore than they did eating the standard American diet once you factor out processed food, snacks, and restaurant meals. Ground beef, eggs, and organ meat are among the most nutrient-dense foods per dollar available in any grocery store. The budget barrier is real for some people, but it's not as fixed as it seems once you know which cuts to buy.
